title: Rav Mari (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: A student of Rava, as in Kiddushin 32b: that Rava was serving drinks at the wedding feast of his son, and handed a cup to Rav Pappa and to Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua, and they stood up before him; and to Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas son of Rav Chisda, and they did not stand up before him. Rava became angry and said: Are these rabbis and those not rabbis? (But some read there: Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, the sons of Rav Chisda.)

He was a colleague of Rav Zevid (a student of Rava), disagreeing with him, as in Bava Batra 96a and 134b and Sotah 40a. And we find in Chullin 117a: Rav Mari said to Rav Zevid ... he said to him: Of you Scripture says, etc.
And in Berakhot 24a, he asked Rav Pappa who answered him jokingly, "hair, hair."
And we find in Zevachim 29b that Rav Ashi raised a difficulty against him, and Hyman infers there that he was like a teacher of Rav Ashi.

So too he is mentioned in Bava Kamma 39b resolving the words of Abaye, and in Yevamot 80a raising an objection against the words of Rav Yosef, and in Ketubot 33b challenging the solutions of Rabbi Yaakov of Nehar Pekod.
And in Shabbat 155b he says the figurative saying: "anoint its [the dog’s] ears, and then a stick behind it,"

notes.text: Berakhot24a explicitly has Rav Mari asking Rav Pappa, so מר״פ here means “from Rav Pappa.” Shabbat155b has “anoint its ears”; Hyman’s supplied אורניה differs from the named text’s אודניה. The small food portion/ears image is retained as a proverb. The variant making both Mari and Pinchas sons of Rav Chisda remains explicit.

Kiddushin 32b directly has the rebuke as a question and uses a singular patronymic for Pinchas; Hyman also reports the plural reading. Berakhot 24a directly has Mari asking Rav Pappa and the “hair, hair” reply. Shabbat 155b has the ears-and-stick image in the small-portion-for-a-dog context. Hyman’s teacher inference about Rav Ashi remains an inference, not a new authority relation.
